security_problem: The repository's verification entry point mutated the tree it was verifying. harness/check.sh ran `make fmt` (`go fmt ./...`), which rewrote tracked files. cmd/visor-workflow binds a task's recorded evidence to a workspace snapshot digest and rejects a later mismatch, so a single unformatted tracked file made an otherwise green task unreachable at HARNESS_VERIFIED with target_snapshot_mismatch. CI had no formatting check either, so drift merged green, and the pre-commit hook did not warn locally.
required_behavior: One check-only script, scripts/check-gofmt, is the single formatting authority: it reports unformatted Go, names the files, and exits non-zero without rewriting anything; it fails closed on a Go file that does not parse; it checks tracked plus untracked-but-not-ignored Go files via git so ignored trees such as .worktrees/ stay out of scope. harness/check.sh calls that script instead of `make fmt`, writes its output into the harness manifest, and runs vet and test unchanged. CI runs the same script in the Lint job. CONTRIBUTING.md tells a contributor that unformatted Go fails the harness and CI and that `make fmt` is the fix. harness/invariants.md records the rule as H51.
failure_behavior: A non-gofmt-clean tree fails the harness, CI and the contract's target command with the offending filenames printed; nothing is reformatted automatically, so evidence keeps binding to the tree it was recorded against. A Go file that cannot be parsed exits non-zero. `make fmt` remains available to developers and is never called from a verification path.
non_goals: Reformatting any file in this change (internal/proxy/proxy.go drift is fixed separately)
Replacing golangci-lint or adding new linters
Changing Makefile targets or the developer `make fmt` workflow
Adding a Go-version assertion beyond using whichever gofmt is first on PATH
Touching any proxy, policy, audit or workflow logic
